pretreatments.description: Shredding (I-PT) – performed using a knife mill at low speed, which reduces the particle size of the substrates.
Shredding and mixing (II-PT) – performed using a pulping operation, which favors the extraction of organic compounds into the liquid phase and combines shredding with mixing.
Shredding, mixing and blending (III-PT) – performed using a fine blending operation, which alters the lignocellulosic structure and creates a homogeneous liquid slurry.

Hammer mill (Noremat Valormax BA915D) – used at an on-farm AD plant (M3) for cattle manure, reducing particle size and increasing methane production kinetics without significantly affecting biodegradability.
Fixed hammer mill – used at an on-farm AD plant (M4) for cattle manure, slightly increasing BMP and methane production kinetics.
Chain mill (X-Chopper) – used at the METHELEC AD plant for the silage and manure mixture (SM), showing a significant impact on BMP and kinetics.
Mixture of cattle manure (M2) – used as raw substrate before pretreatment and as part of the lab-scale SM sample, characterized for physical and biochemical properties.
Mixture of maize and triticale silage (S) – used as raw substrate and in the lab-scale SM sample, characterized for physical and biochemical properties.
Mixture of silage S and cattle manure (SM) – used as raw substrate and in the lab-scale SM sample, characterized for physical and biochemical properties.

Storage at 4 °C (implied storage treatment) – applied to samples from farm M2, Ennezat, causing significant degradation of organic soluble compounds and reducing biodegradability compared to fresh samples.
Shredding and mixing at full scale (HM3) – used at the on-farm AD plant (La Bouzule) for cattle manure, resulting in particle size reduction and kinetic enhancement.
Shredding and mixing at full scale (HM4) – used at the on-farm AD plant (M4) for cattle manure, resulting in slight BMP increase and kinetic enhancement.
Chain milling at full scale (CH-SM) – used at the METHELEC AD plant for the silage and manure mixture (SM), resulting in significant BMP increase and kinetic enhancement.
Liquid leaching test (10:1 water/TS ratio for 2 hours with constant bottle rotation) – performed during sample preparation to separate liquid and particulate fractions before characterization.
Centrifugation (20 min at 5000 G) – performed on samples after leaching to separate supernatant and particulate fractions.
Particulate fraction drying (70 °C for 3 days and calcination at 550 °C for 2 hours) – performed on the remaining solid fraction to determine Total Solids (TS), Volatile Solids (VS), and COD.
Water retention capacity (WRC) measurement – performed following Coarita Fernandez et al. method (water contact with substrate in a column for 2 hours) on all raw and pre-treated samples.
Particle size distribution analysis using wet sieving method (sieve openings: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 4, 10, 20.0, and 31.5 mm) and drying at 105 °C for 24 hours on all samples.

Biomethane potential (BMP) testing – carried out in mesophilic conditions (35 °C) with 80/20 %v N2/CO2 purging and monitoring of daily methane production to determine ultimate maximal biochemical methane potential.
Biomethane potential kinetics testing – conducted simultaneously with BMP tests to fit first-order kinetic models for methane production.
Biochemical Methane Potential (BMP) estimation – calculated from BMP and COD measurements using the formula: BMP [L_STP/kg VS] × COD [g_COD/kg VS] × 0.35.
COD (Chemical Oxygen Demand) measurement – performed following NF U 44–161 and NF ISO 14235 standards on both particulate and water-soluble fractions.
pH measurement – performed using a Consort C3020 device with a SP10B pH-electrode on water-soluble fraction samples.
Volatile Solids (VS) content determination – performed through 105 °C drying for 24h and calcination at 550 °C for 2h with correction using volatilization coefficients.
Water soluble fraction analysis – performed on supernatant samples after leaching to measure Total solids (TS), Volatile Solids (VS), BMP, pH, and COD.
Total solids (TS) content measurement – performed on the particulate fraction after drying at 70 °C for 3 days.
